title: PDL Week 3 | Season 8 | 2026
coldOpen: Week 2 gave us 188 from Wichita, 174 from Southern Oregon, and Max opening the garage sale after one loss. Mobile-Wheelchair Marv caught zero passes, Joe nearly doubled his score, and Greg finally got Rome just in time to lose by 60. Welcome to Week 3 of the PDL Power Rankings.

1: I had a bye this week.
Delco won 124.46 to 28.30, and somehow I came out of Sunday more annoyed with my team than I was before it started.
Mostly because the receiver room I spent all offseason convincing myself was deep continues to look like dog-shit.
Smitty gets a pass; shockingly, Diggs does too.
Everyone else can explain themselves.
Jamo caught two balls for 33 yards.
Think of the amount of gaslighting I had to do after his Week 1 performance. No way they keep him this uninvolved again, right?
Oh Tommy, you dumb piece of shit.
DK has the opposite problem. They keep throwing him the ball and absolutely nothing happens.
Nine targets against New England.
Four catches.
27 yards.
And he had two catches for two yards until Pittsburgh was already down 20-3 and New England started playing prevent.
So apparently the key to unlocking DK Metcalf is making sure the game is already over.
DK called the offense “very frustrating” afterward.
Maybe if you learned to catch the ball, it wouldn't be as frustrating, buddy.
And then there is Mitsubishi Marv.
How much time do we have?
Zero catches.
One target.
The anonymous mailbag last week asked if Marvin Harrison Jr. was just Black Alec Pierce.
At the time, I thought this was an attack on me personally.
Two weeks into the season, Pierce has 97 receiving yards.
Marv has 33.
Pierce just got hurt, but at this point I'm genuinely interested in seeing how long he can stay ahead from IR.
Arizona fans are already losing their minds over this. Harrison has four targets through two games and just finished an entire NFL game without a catch.
I gave up Derrick Henry and a first for him.
Henry has 212 rushing yards and four touchdowns.
Marv has caught one football.
One.
The Derrick Henry trade currently looks less like buying low and more like I accidentally participated in a Make-A-Wish for Arizona.
Tyler Shough also put 24.38 on my bench while leading the NFL in passing, because God continues to bless Delco exclusively at quarterback.
Naturally, the one position I have absolutely no problems at.
Thank God Joe was on the schedule.
2: Week 1: 15 points.
Joe nearly doubled his score.
If this continues, Connecticut will put up 56.6 next week, 113.2 the week after that, and 226.4 by Week 5.
So really, everybody needs to enjoy this while they can.
Unfortunately, 28.3 was still not enough to beat 124.
Tyjae Spears led the entire lineup with eight points. Three starters scored zero. Another two failed to reach three.
Jalen Royals scored 7.6 on the bench.
He would’ve been Connecticut’s second-highest scorer.
Depth.
Keenan Allen is also still here, which I genuinely did not expect.

I thought Jeff would have acquired him by now after losing A.J. Brown. Instead, Keenan gave Joe one catch for five yards this week and continues to age in real time on a roster that has absolutely no use for him.
The sell window is getting smaller every Sunday.
At some point Joe is going to message the league “Keenan for a third?” and get six thumbs-down reactions without a single counter.
Then there’s Tyson Bagent.
Caleb Williams hurt his hamstring against Minnesota and got carted off looking like we might not see him again until Christmas.
Then Monday came around and suddenly the reports were encouraging and he might barely miss any time.
Can someone remind Caleb he’s playing football, not futbol.
Joe mentioned Bagent might actually be good.
Naturally, Bagent is also on the Crocs.
He came in after Caleb got hurt and nearly got Chicago back into the game.
Joe believes in Bagent because he may roster him. I believe in Bagent because his dad is Travis Bagent, a world champion arm wrestler.
We are not the same.
Honestly, if anybody has the bloodline to drag this roster all the way to 2027, it might be him.
Tank Commander Bagent is ready to roll.
3: Jeff finally got the week he spent all offseason trying to buy.
Highest score in the league.

And the anticlimactic part is he did it while Saquon basically missed the game. Barkley left with a shoulder stinger, finished with four carries for nine yards, and gave Wichita 2.5 points. A.J. Brown is already on IR. Zay Flowers didn’t play.
This was supposed to be the part where all those expensive veterans started making Jeff a little uncomfortable.
Instead, he had 152.86 points before Davante Adams even played Monday night.
Brian finished with 104.58.
Davante could have stayed home.
He did not.
Eight catches. 195 yards. Two touchdowns.
35.5 points for Jeff.
And because apparently just ruining Brian’s Monday wasn’t enough, Davante also moved into the top 25 in NFL history in career receiving yards.
I was already halfway to mentally trading Keenan Allen from Joe to Wichita after A.J. Brown went down. Jeff’s receiver depth finally looked like the one place you could poke at this roster.
Davante drops 35.
Tre Tucker puts another 20.4 on the bench.
Keenan can stay with Joe and continue whatever the hell is happening over there.
Sunday night was worse.
Jeff had Mahomes, Kelce and Kenneth Walker all going in Chiefs-Colts.
Mahomes threw for 382 and three touchdowns. Kelce went 9 for 101 and a touchdown. Walker had 178 yards from scrimmage.
Then the game went to overtime because apparently Wichita needed the extra possessions.
80.88 fantasy points from the three of them.
Brian could have added another Hollywood Hu$tle to his lineup and still lost.
And Kelce casually used the night to pass Marshall Faulk for the most career yards after catch in NFL history.
So the old guys Jeff spent all offseason buying are not exactly limping toward retirement.
They’re breaking NFL records while his expensive running back scores 2.5.
I don’t have much else for Jeff this week.

Some made fun of the spending. Some wondered what happens when the injuries start. Some wondered if he had enough receiver depth. Some wondered whether turning years of rebuilding into a pile of older stars was going to blow up in his face.
Week 2’s answer was 188.36.
Apparently the cliff is somewhere past Marshall Faulk.
4: Max lasted one week.

All offseason he got annoyed whenever somebody suggested MSE might not be as good as he thought. Darren questioned the roster, Max came back with ages and rankings and basically every piece of evidence short of a sworn affidavit.
Then Week 1 happened.
Chase Brown: gone.
Dak Prescott: gone.
By the time we recorded the podcast, Greg had already referred to Max as the first owner to wave the white flag.
The Chase trade I actually like for him. Max turned Brown and a fourth into Michael Wilson plus Jon’s 2027 second and third.
Richmond just scored 26 points and owns no first next year.
I’d probably want those picks too.
It’s also Chase Brown, though.
Darren called him one of those players “only Max really likes” during the preseason rankings and Max spent days arguing about it.
Apparently Darren just needed to wait until September.
Dak was next.
We joked on the podcast that Welch made too much sense as a landing spot. He needed a quarterback. His team is literally called Dallas Drip. His co-owner is a Cowboys fan.
So naturally Max sent him Dak for Bryce Young and two thirds.
The Oregon pipeline is alive and well.
Dak’s first Sunday as a member of Dallas Drip: 279 yards, four touchdowns, Cowboys win, and he passes Tony Romo for the most touchdown passes in franchise history.
Excellent timing, Max.
Fortunately, Bryce decided to make this significantly less funny for us.
287 yards. Three touchdowns. Carolina wins 34-3.
He’s now thrown three touchdowns in both games this season and apparently owns a timeshare in Mercedes-Benz Stadium.
So Max traded away the quarterback who became the Cowboys’ all-time touchdown leader and acquired the quarterback currently treating Atlanta like a home game.
Annoyingly, both sides of this worked immediately.
Max now has Bryce and Cam Ward instead of Dak and Stroud as the long-term QB picture, Michael Wilson is here, and he added four future picks in the two deals.
Ja’Marr isn’t going anywhere. Ladd isn’t going anywhere. Max already told Greg Coker isn’t for sale. Carnell Tate just got here.
This isn’t Jon or Joe where the goal is to make Sundays completely irrelevant for two years.
It just turns out the guy who spent August insisting he was a dark horse was also the first contender to start cashing pieces out.
MSE beat Dubrovnik this week, but Brett scored 53 points. That’s not really the story.
Max spent the offseason arguing that we were all too low on his roster.
Two weeks later he has Bryce Young, Michael Wilson and a small stack of Jon’s future draft picks.
He could have saved himself a lot of arguing in August by just telling us that was the plan.
5: Joe outscored Jon.
Not in 2027 picks.
In actual fantasy points.

Connecticut: 28.3
Richmond: 26.4
Joe owns eight firsts next year and is actively fielding a tank roster. Jon owns zero because he pushed so much into this rookie class.
That’s a rough scoreboard to look at on Tuesday morning.
Makai Lemon did technically improve.
Week 1: -5 yards.
Through Week 2: 9 yards total.
Two NFL games in and Lemon is one yard short of having traveled the full length of an end zone.
Baby steps.

Antonio Williams came back down after being Richmond’s leading scorer last week. Kenyon Sadiq followed his opening-week touchdown with two catches for 17 yards. Omar Cooper and Jordyn Tyson are still hurt.
Fernando Mendoza remains completely healthy, mostly because nobody has allowed him onto the football field yet.
Kirko has been cookin.
Three more touchdowns, Vegas is 2-0, and suddenly every Kohl’s in the greater Las Vegas area is reporting record foot traffic.
This was never supposed to be a winning season for Richmond. Losing to Brian or whoever doesn’t really matter.
Getting outscored by Joe absolutely does.
Jon needs this season to start giving him some evidence that the class he bought into is going somewhere. Yes, it has been two weeks. Yes, manufacturing drama is what I do.
So far the return is nine Makai Lemon receiving yards, a quarterback holding a clipboard, two injured receivers and Kenyon Sadiq.
Meanwhile Joe’s roster is intentionally terrible.
That’s what makes this so funny.
One team is supposed to look unfinished.
The other one just lost to it.
6: Darren’s Hollywood playoff guarantee survived exactly one game and one Wednesday practice.
Before Week 1: Brian will make the playoffs.
Nico Collins tweaks his hamstring at practice.
Next podcast: “Maybe Brian doesn’t make the playoffs.”
Darren, stand up.
We bullied him into actually putting a hot take on record and the man started backing away from it before Week 2 even kicked off.
To be fair, Nico is the player Brian went out and paid a 2027 first for when he decided Hollywood was competing again. He gave Brian 17.7 in Week 1, then the hamstring flared up and he missed Sunday.
Now he’s looking unlikely for Week 3 too, which is especially comforting considering he already missed five games with a hamstring injury in 2024.
Houston is 0-2, Nico’s hamstring is already acting up, and Brian has a future first tied up in this.
Darren may have just been early.
Hollywood at least didn’t immediately fall apart without him.
Parker Washington gave Brian another 13.3 and is becoming a consistent fixture.
We spent the preseason making fun of Brian because every third player on his roster had apparently been the subject of some glowing training camp report. Parker was one of the main offenders.
Then he went out against Denver, got 12 targets and finished with 98 yards. He now has 181 receiving yards through two games.
Alright, Brian.
You got one.
This is terrible news for everybody who has spent the last month ignoring the Jaguars clips he sends us.
Josh Downs gave him 10.7. Egbuka continues to be useful. Tuten had 13.2. Malik Willis gave him 14.48 in the superflex.
Willis got sacked four times while Miami lost 35-13 and still gave Brian a usable fantasy day.

This was exactly where I thought Hollywood would get into trouble once somebody important went down, and instead Brian’s collection of random preseason crushes is actually holding the roster together.
We also spent part of the podcast asking whether Nico’s injury would change Brian’s plans.
All three of us eventually said no.
Which sounds confident until you remember this is Brian.
This is the same owner who has gone from competing, to reloading, back to competing in roughly the time it takes most of us to negotiate one trade.
Nico misses another week? Maybe Brian waits.
Hollywood keeps hanging around without him? Maybe Brian starts shopping.
Three straight losses?
Check back at lunch.
I own Brian’s 2027 first, so I have a very simple request.
Darren, please stop speaking this playoff appearance into existence.
7: Things have to feel pretty good in Philly right now.
2-0. 154.66 points. Stafford back from the jetlag. CeeDee back to being CeeDee. Kittle healthy. Gibbs doing Gibbs things.
Darren beat Greg by almost 60 and did it with DJ Moore scoring negative 0.1.
Honestly, start him again. Maybe he can get to negative one next week and make this interesting.
Stafford was the bigger development.
After giving Darren 3.1 in Week 1, he came back Monday night with 327 yards, four touchdowns and 33.98 points.
Apparently the cure for jetlag was getting the Giants.
He also moved into sixth all-time in career passing touchdowns, which is a pretty dramatic improvement from whatever the hell Week 1 was.
CeeDee bounced back too. 153 yards, two touchdowns, 31.3 points.
At that point Kittle, Gibbs and Garrett Wilson were basically just running up the score.
Even Deshaun Watson put 23.72 on Darren’s bench.
Actually, that whole quarterback room had a weirdly productive Sunday.
Watson and Baker played each other in Tampa, Watson won, and Darren owned both of them while Stafford was waiting to throw four touchdowns Monday night.
Which makes the Dak rumor even more interesting.
Darren was reportedly sniffing around Dak before Welch got him.
This roster currently has Stafford, Baker, Darnold, Tua, Anthony Richardson and Deshaun Watson.
Naturally, Darren looked at that and thought: maybe one more.
To be fair, I get it. Stafford looked ancient in Week 1, Darnold and Tua are already hurt, Richardson is basically decorative, and Baker hasn’t looked that great since the first half of last season.
But Stafford throwing four touchdowns while Deshaun beats Baker on Darren’s bench probably buys everyone a week.
For now there really isn’t much to complain about.
He’s 2-0, just dropped 154, Stafford looked like himself again, CeeDee looked ridiculous, and Darren finally got to beat Greg badly enough that he went MIA.
Probably already has the podcast notes open.
8: Welch saw Minivan Marv put up a goose egg and immediately got brave in the chat.
I was going to respond, but then I opened his matchup.
So instead I have spent the morning looking for red flags.
I found several.
First, Welch traded for Dak Prescott and Dak immediately threw four touchdowns, beat Washington, and passed Tony Romo for the most touchdown passes in Cowboys history.
Sounds great until you realize he still wasn’t the best quarterback on Welch’s team.
Jared Goff: 37.78.
Dak Prescott: 37.76.
Imagine finally getting the Cowboys quarterback on a team called Dallas Drip and he can’t even win the job by Tuesday.
Concerning.
Goff threw four touchdowns of his own Thursday night. Amon-Ra had 142 yards and two scores.
So now we’re supposed to be impressed because Welch’s Lions stack combined for almost 70?
I see dependency issues.
Trey McBride only scored 18.1.
No touchdown.
Very troubling lack of upside.
Christian Watson couldn’t even crack 13.
David Montgomery scored 3.4, which I believe is the first piece of legitimate evidence I’ve found that Dallas is actually bad.
Thank you, David.
Unfortunately, the NFL drug-tested CeeDee Lamb after he went for 153 and two touchdowns in that same Cowboys game.
Welch, I’ll need a urine sample by Thursday.
Because 165 points against Jon is frankly unsportsmanlike.
Richmond scored 26.4.
Welch had three players individually come within ten points of Jon’s entire lineup.
Running up the score on a rebuilding team and then coming into the chat to shit on Moped Marv?
Classless.
And I know what Welch is going to say.
Dak looked great. Goff looked great. Amon-Ra looked great. McBride is still McBride. The roster just put up 165.
Whatever.
Marv has 33 receiving yards this season and I’m not emotionally prepared to have this conversation on the merits.
So I’m going with conduct detrimental to the league.
9: Greg finally got Rome Odunze.

It only took 46 trade offers and about two years of bothering Mike. Greg said on the podcast he had already started looking for a jersey and autographed cards before we even finished talking about the trade.
So I’m honestly not sure he noticed Darren beat him by 60.
Philadelphia 154.66. London 94.80.
If it weren't for the acquisition of Rome, this would be Greggy's 9/11.
Losing to Darren and then having to listen to Darren talk about it...I'm not sure Greg will be on the next pod.
Rome’s long-awaited Monarchs debut was three catches for 48 yards.
5.8 points.
Forty-six offers.
I’m not saying anything else. The man waited long enough.
I picked London to win the league before the season and I’m not doing the Darren thing where one bad week happens and suddenly I’m walking back my hot take.
I am, however, staring at Justin Herbert a little harder than I expected.
I was pretty bought into Mike McDaniel getting there and making Herbert’s life easier. Quick game, motion, get the ball out, stop asking him to survive every dropback like he did last year.
Two games in, Herbert looks like shit.
Against Vegas: 192 yards, one touchdown, two picks, three fumbles.
The Chargers are 0-2 after losing to Arizona and Las Vegas, two teams that went a combined 6-28 last year.
Greg waited two years for Rome and somehow Justin Herbert is the one testing his patience.
Now Buffalo, Seattle, Denver and Kansas City are next.
My current coping mechanism is that Herbert spends the next month down 17 points and throwing the ball 45 times.
This is fantasy football. I don’t need the Chargers to fix anything. I need garbage time.
The running backs couldn’t bail Greg out this time either. Bijan, Henry and Breece combined for 37.5 after dropping 80.9 in Week 1.
Still fine.
Just considerably less fun when your two quarterbacks combine for 22.88.
Greg had another 20 from Jake Ferguson sitting on the bench and useful days from Bateman and Geno too, so the roster depth is still very obviously there.
The Darren loss is ugly. Herbert worries me. I still think the roster is loaded.
And Greg finally has Rome.
He probably had a perfectly nice Sunday.
10: Greg spent two years and 46 trade offers trying to get Rome Odunze.
Offer 46 finally worked.
Greg got Rome.
Mike got Chris Olave.
Olave’s first game for Southern Oregon: eight catches, 86 yards, a touchdown, 18.6 points.
Mike beat the defending champ 174.30 to 149.66.
He could have left Olave on the bench and still won.
Great. Glad we are all participating this season.
The roster was already stupid before Greg decided to help.

Josh Allen opened Buffalo’s new stadium with five touchdowns and handed Mike 46.82 on Thursday night. Three through the air, two on the ground, 69 rushing yards because apparently the passing stuff wasn’t enough.
Apparently Allen was sick enough before the game to need IV fluids and was still throwing up.
Mike’s quarterback can apparently play through the flu better than most of our rosters can play healthy.
By Sunday, FOX was having trouble keeping track.
Howie Long said Allen had ten touchdowns through two weeks, then immediately listed five passing and four rushing.
Michael Strahan had to remind him that five plus four is nine.
Mike got 46.82 either way.
Then his other quarterback went 20-of-22 against Miami.
Brock Purdy threw for 287, ran for another 30 and scored three times while San Francisco scored touchdowns on its first five possessions.
79.3 points from Mike’s quarterbacks.
His QB2 missed two passes.
Great league.
And this wasn’t even everybody hitting.
Justin Jefferson scored seven.
George Pickens scored seven.
Jeanty had 8.3.
Achane had 10.8.
Mike still scored 174.
Olave came over and immediately gave him 18.6. Waddle had 17.8. LaPorta had 17.2.
Dalton Schultz scored 26 on the bench, which feels like exactly the kind of thing Mike will still find a way to be irritated about.
That’s really the only entertainment left here.
Southern Oregon is 2-0.
Mike has scored 332.56 points in two weeks.
So now we wait.
George Pickens has scored exactly seven points in both games.
I give it until lunch before he’s on Mike’s trade block.
By dinner every offer will be rejected.
By tomorrow Pickens will be unavailable.
11: Brett spent the offseason saying he wanted to bring back the Purdue nickname.
You have to actually spoil somebody’s season first, Brett.
Dubrovnik is 0-2 and just lost 114.90 to 53.46 to the guy who spent the week selling Chase Brown and Dak Prescott.
Maybe let’s get within 60 before we dust off “Spoilermakers.”

Week 1 at least gave Brett something to puff his chest out about. Dart dropped 32.6, Lawrence dropped 34.1, and I had to eat shit after spending half the podcast explaining why I didn’t trust the Giants offense.
One week later, Dart made it three passes into Monday night before leaving with what is believed to be an MCL sprain.
0.8 points.
Cool.
And apparently Brett’s roster decided one injury wasn’t enough.
JK Dobbins left with a hamstring injury. Alec Pierce hurt the same foot he had surgery on this offseason and left Arrowhead in a boot and on crutches.
Colston Loveland is fine though.
Physically.
Two games.
One catch.
Three receiving yards.
The league has it out for MHJ, and rightfully so. This man is single-handedly destroying my mental health, but Marv has 11 times as many receiving yards as Loveland.
The Bears went from scoring 59 in Week 1 to scoring three points in Week 2, and somehow Loveland has managed to match the Week 2 team total with his entire season.

There are still reasons Brett was excited about this roster in the first place. Omarion Hampton finally had a week that looked more like what you wanted when you drafted him. Tet continues to look legit. Boston popped for 18 on the bench. The young guys Brett actually needs long-term are not all combusting at once.
And this is also the risk Brett willingly signed up for when he kept telling us this wasn’t the year.
Carnell Tate gone.
Jaden Reed gone (I could have phrased this better)
Keep pushing value forward, let the kids develop, worry about actually winning later.
Fair enough.
But if you’re going to spend August getting horny about bringing back the Purdue nickname, somebody eventually has to get upset.
Right now Dubrovnik is getting blown out by an owner who started liquidating his roster after one week.
Put Purdue back in storage.
12: Tanish scored 149.66 this week and lost by almost 25.
Top-five score in the league. Happened to draw Mike, who put up 174.30.
The schedule Gods are unforgiving.
The more annoying part is Tanish spent basically the entire offseason trying to trade one of Caleb Williams, Jayden Daniels or Drake Maye because carrying all three felt excessive.
Two weeks in, he might need all three.

Daniels dislocated the same left elbow that cost him most of the end of last season and isn’t expected to play Week 3. Caleb’s injury thankfully came back much better than it looked, but he’s still week-to-week with a Grade 1 hamstring strain.
That leaves Drake Maye.
7.02 points.
Problem solved.
Tanish also traded for Chase Brown this week because apparently the Boulder Bears did not have enough running backs.
I count twelve on this roster.
Chase’s debut: 20 carries for 80 yards, three catches for two yards, 9.7 points.
Good.
Number twelve is settling in nicely.
Meanwhile, one of the few wide receivers Tanish actually does need gave him 0.6.

Malik Nabers caught one ball for ten yards Monday night. Jaxson Dart hurt his MCL on the opening drive, Nabers hurt his shoulder later, came back, and then spent the rest of the night catching passes from Jameis Winston in a game where the Giants scored six points.
Maybe trading for another running back really was the move.
Thankfully, JSN decided none of this was going to matter.
Nine catches. 155 yards. Three touchdowns. 38 points.
Drew Lock’s first pass of the game went 82 yards to JSN for a touchdown.
The funny part is it wasn’t even supposed to be a go route. JSN beat the corner so badly that Lock basically looked up and said fuck it.
He scored two more after that.
Apparently being the reigning Offensive Player of the Year means the play call is more of a suggestion.
Jonathan Taylor added 27.2. Kincaid had 22.5. Daniels still managed 16.74 before his elbow went.
That’s enough.
Tanish lost, dropped to 1-1, has two injured quarterbacks, Nabers coming out of the Monday night Giants infirmary, and got 9.7 from running back number twelve.
He still scored 149.66.
The defending champs get disrespected, so maybe it's finally time he makes an appearance with Brian and Brett?
